facts.fact: ARTICLE 19's UPR statement refers to Rwanda's existing Access to Information Law and says compliance with it is not independently monitored.
ARTICLE 19 says no independent oversight body has been established to monitor compliance with the Access to Information Law since the Ombudsman's ATI mandate was removed.

RWA.note: The document states nothing on digital financial services.

facts.fact: ARTICLE 19 lists the enactment of the Data Protection and Privacy law among Rwanda's steps in the review cycle, without saying whether it is in force.
ARTICLE 19 says independent online news sites including The Rwandan and Le Prophete, and local diaspora platforms, remain blocked.
ARTICLE 19 says journalists and online commentators continue to face arrests and prosecutions for speech offences, and several independent YouTube-based journalists have been detained or intimidated.
facts.system: Speech offences in the Penal Code

RWA.note: The statement names CIPESA and the University of Birmingham as co-authors of a submission; neither is shown as a Rwanda-based institution.
